issue.author: qa
issue.body:
I need, to check each build against the objective (title, arrow-key turning, growth + score, wall/self collision, game-over score, play again):
- The path of the page to open (e.g. index.html at repo root) and how it is served (static file or a command).
- Ideally a read-only state hook for headless tests, e.g. `window.__snake = {state:'title|playing|gameover', score, snake:[{x,y}...], food:{x,y}, grid:{cols,rows}}`, or equivalent data-attributes / DOM ids for the score and screens. Without it I can only check by screenshots/pixels, which is weaker.
- Whether the tick speed can be set (e.g. a URL param like ?speed=fast, or a documented constant) so tests do not take long.
Waiting on this: the automated test script; I will start checking as soon as a first build is pushed. Please say where these are documented (e.g. docs/testing.md).
issue.title: QA: entry point and test hooks for the Snake build

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
Everything you asked for is in commit 78f16e43e892da6e97db091d3eb93d128a8b45ed and release **v0.2.0** (`snake-v0.2.0.zip`, the assembled delivery including the artist's assets). It's documented in `docs/testing.md`:

- **Entry point:** `index.html` at the delivery root. It's a static page with no build step. Open it as `file://…/index.html` or serve the folder (`python3 -m http.server 8000`).
- **Read-only state:** `window.__snake` has `state` (`'title' | 'playing' | 'paused' | 'over'`, where `over` is the game-over screen), `score` (the final score once the game is over), `best`, `snake` (`[{x,y}]`, head first), `food` (`{x,y}`), `grid` (`{cols:20, rows:20, cell:32}`), `interval` (ms per tick) and `game.cause` (`'wall' | 'self'`). The canvas `#game` also has `data-state` and `data-score` attributes.
- **Speed:** `index.html?speed=<ms>` fixes the tick length (minimum 10 ms). The default is 130 ms, 2 ms faster per point, never below 70 ms.
- **Optional manual stepping:** `__snake.setAuto(false)` stops the timer, and `__snake.tick()` then advances exactly one cell.
- **Already checked on the unzipped v0.2.0:** my own checks are `tests/test_game.py` (26/26 passed) and `tests/test_play.py` (real-time, keyboard only, `?speed=90`: ate 5 foods, wall death, replay, no console errors). Screenshots are in `tests/shots/`.

This covers what your test script needs for R1–R8. Please report defects as issues here.

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
Confirmed: the game uses your proposal and your files as they are (commit 168dbb55bb376666aa61632057c92f126ef20e2f). Nothing needs renaming. The game is now on a **32 px cell** grid of 20×20, so the play area is 640×640 under a 48 px score bar. Release **v0.2.0** of `world/game-developer` contains the game with your assets. Screenshots from the running game are in `tests/shots/` of my repo (`1-title.png`, `2-play.png`, `3-gameover-wall.png`, `4-gameover-self.png`, `5-realtime-play.png`).

`docs/assets.md` in my repo describes exactly how each file is used. In short:
- The four head sprites are chosen by direction.
- `body.png` is used for every segment and for the tail. It's rotated 90° on vertical runs and drawn unrotated at corners.
- `bg_tile_pair.png` is the checkerboard: left half on even cells, right half on odd cells.
- `title_logo.png` is scaled to fit 560×160.
- `gameover_panel.png` is drawn at 360×200. I write the final score and best score into its lower half, and the play-again prompt below it.
- `eat`, `start` and `gameover` WAVs play on those events.

The game requests only these files, so the console stays free of 404 errors. If you add a `tail.png` (body continuing to the right) or a `body_turn.png` (corner joining the right and bottom edges), the drawing code already supports them. Tell me here and I'll add them to the load list.

issue.author: producer
issue.body:
**What I need:** a playtest report on the Snake build to play #1 — the assembled delivery that is the release candidate.

**Where:** release `play-1` in `world/producer`, file `snake-build-1.zip` (`forge api repos/world/producer/releases/tags/play-1` gives its `browser_download_url`; download with `curl -fLo snake-build-1.zip -u "$HT_FORGEJO_USER:$FORGEJO_TOKEN" <url>`). Unzip into an empty directory and open `index.html` (works from `file://` or a static server). Contents: `game-developer` 78f16e43e892da6e97db091d3eb93d128a8b45ed + `artist` assets f5b3b5d5cf2c3a738eea4a39c596ce2e4925a0bf.

**What it is for:** acceptance of the release. My standard (`ht-role brief`, R1–R9) requires a playtester report on the same build before I approve; it is the only input still missing.

**What I already know:** I played it headless (title → Enter → ate 5 foods, +1 length/+1 point each → death on a wall and on itself → replay by Enter and by click; reverse key ignored; no console errors; page didn't scroll). QA's v0.2.0 run found 56/56 pass. What I don't have is a player's view: is it clear how to start and replay, does the pace feel right (130 ms/tick, speeding up 2 ms per point down to 70 ms), are the controls responsive, is anything confusing or frustrating (e.g. the 0.4 s guard before replay works), do the head/body/food/board read clearly, are sounds OK if you can check them.

**Waiting on it:** my approval of the release. Please state the build you played (release `play-1`), pass/fail per point with screenshots, and anything that should block release, then close this issue.
issue.title: Playtest the release candidate: build to play #1 (release play-1 in producer)

comments.author: playtester
comments.body:
Playtest report for release play-1 (snake-build-1.zip; game-developer 78f16e43, artist f5b3b5d5) is pushed: playtest/play-1.md at 7d568de1d5587e3e828a58876a2711f722fab4c0, with screenshots in playtest/shots/ and a session recording playtest/play-1-session.webm.

Played in headless Chromium with real key/mouse events at the normal pace, no console errors. R1–R9 all PASS: title → start, reverse key ignored, +1 length/+1 point per food, wall death and self death, game-over screen with final score, replay by Enter and by click, pause works, no page scroll. Nothing should block release.

Minor, non-blocking notes: a third arrow key pressed within one tick is dropped (turn queue is capped at 2); the game-over veil hides what the snake hit; the wall is only a thin border line. Sound was checked only as files (no clipping), not listened to in a browser. Closing.
